title: Perks or Payments?
topic: An original fictional finance short about comparing real rewards with fees and interest. No named card offers or promised savings.

sources.claim: Annual fees should be compared with the benefits received; interest costs also matter when carrying a balance.
sources.excerpt: Ask yourself if any benefits or rewards you get with the card are worth the fee.

sources.claim: The CFPB reports that revolving-balance consumers often pay more interest and fees than they receive in rewards.
sources.excerpt: Consumers who carry revolving balances often pay far more in interest and fees than they get back on rewards.

patterns: Transcript describes studying successful channels before original research, scripts, storyboards and production.

scenes.speaker: dave
scenes.narration: My rewards card deserves a trophy. So why is my wallet asking for a fire extinguisher?
scenes.visual: Dave proudly holds a card; a red bill interrupts his victory pose.

scenes.speaker: points_monk
scenes.narration: Because the trophy is not paying the bill. Compare benefits you actually use with the annual fee.
scenes.visual: Points Monk turns the card into an itemized value-versus-fee receipt.

scenes.speaker: dave
scenes.narration: But it comes with perks. And a very impressive rectangle.
scenes.visual: Dave tries to defend the rectangle; Monk holds an empty checklist.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.narration: Carrying a balance changes the math. Interest and fees can outweigh the rewards.
scenes.visual: A level balance diagram contrasts value and cost; the headline explains that costs can outweigh rewards.

scenes.speaker: points_monk
scenes.narration: Check the fee, the interest rate, and the benefits you will use. Judge the card by the numbers.
scenes.visual: Monk ticks three clearly labeled boxes; Dave lowers the trophy.

scenes.speaker: dave
scenes.narration: Okay. The trophy can stay. The card has to earn its spot.
scenes.visual: Dave places the card beside a checklist instead of on a pedestal.
